author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected. Opening it for correction shows its current date and description; submitting valid values updates that same visit in place and shows the owner's record. A blank description or a date of today or earlier is refused, and the form is redisplayed.
acceptance_criteria: Opening an existing visit for correction prefills the form with that visit's current date and description
Submitting a valid description and a date later than today updates that same visit in place, adds no additional visit to the pet, and shows the owner's record
Submitting a blank description is refused, the description is named, and the form is redisplayed
Submitting a date of today or earlier is refused, the date is named, and the form is redisplayed
non_goals: Cancelling or removing a booked visit stays out of scope (NG-5, narrowed)
notes: Validation matches visit booking (REQ-VIS-001): description required, date later than today. The correction is in place — the pet gains no new visit record. Narrows NG-5; decision path in adr/2026-08-07-non-goal-cancel-visit.md.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction reuses the established owner aggregate write-path (system-design.md Overview + Contracts: 'writes to pets and visits go through OwnerRepository', 'Owner is the aggregate entry point'). No VisitRepository is introduced. In-place update is achieved by binding the form onto the EXISTING Visit instance already resident in pet.getVisits(), located by visitId, and NOT calling pet.addVisit/owner.addVisit. That Visit already carries a non-null id and is already a member of the pet's collection, so owners.save(owner) cascades a JPA UPDATE to the existing row - no INSERT, no new collection member. BaseEntity overrides neither equals nor hashCode, so Set membership is identity-based: mutating the resident instance keeps pet.visits at one member with a stable hash bucket. This mirrors the in-place update the owner/pet edit flows (REQ-OWN-004, REQ-PET-004) already demonstrate, so it adds a flow without a new pattern. The one small adjustment (why minor, not covered) is the shared @ModelAttribute loader collision described under integration_points.
integration_points: The URL is GET/POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit, added to VisitController; the template pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm and its 'visit' model attribute are reused unchanged.

@ModelAttribute('visit') loadPetWithVisit runs before EVERY mapping in VisitController and unconditionally does new Visit() + pet.addVisit(visit). For an edit mapping in the same controller this seeds a spurious new visit. The edit's model-attribute population must instead locate and return the EXISTING visit by visitId and NOT add. Recommended: make the loader path-aware on an optional visitId (present -> find the resident visit, return it, no add; absent -> current booking behavior). A thin Pet.getVisit(Integer id) helper mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id) is the natural home for the lookup and keeps the controller free of collection-walking - consistent with the aggregate-navigation pattern already in Owner.

Validation parity with booking (REQ-VIS-001): reuse @NotBlank description on Visit and replicate the inline non-future-date check result.rejectValue('date','typeMismatch.visitDate') that processNewVisitForm applies; on validation failure return 'pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm'. On success redirect:/owners/{ownerId}.

On edit GET the existing visit's date and description prefill via the returned model attribute; the future-defaulting Visit() constructor and minVisitDate are booking conveniences and are not used to seed the edit form.

patterns.description: processNewVisitForm: the booking POST whose validation (non-future date reject + @Valid) the edit POST mirrors, minus the addVisit/new-instance seeding
Owner.getPet(Integer id): aggregate-navigation lookup-by-id pattern to mirror as Pet.getVisit(Integer id)

risks.risk: LOAD-BEARING: edit path binds onto a fresh Visit or calls addVisit, so save(owner) INSERTs a second visit and the pet gains an extra record - violates the acceptance criterion.
risks.mitigation: Bind the form onto the resident Visit instance located by visitId; never call addVisit on the edit path. Assert in processVisitEditFormSuccess that the pet's visit count is unchanged after the update.

risks.risk: visitId (untrusted path input) does not belong to the addressed pet/owner - id tampering could target another owner's visit.
risks.mitigation: Resolve the visit only by navigating owner -> pet -> visit through the aggregate; a miss fails closed with the same IllegalArgumentException pattern loadPetWithVisit already uses for a missing pet. Scoping the lookup through the path-addressed pet prevents cross-owner edits via id substitution.

risks.risk: Visit id mass-assignment via a hidden form field.
risks.mitigation: The existing @InitBinder setDisallowedFields('id','*.id') already blocks it; the target visit must be derived from the path visitId, never a form field. Reuse the binder as-is.

notes: No autofix records to audit. Indexed the non-goal ADR 2026-08-07-non-goal-cancel-visit.md into docs/adr/README.md (README is a standard ADR doc I own; product-requirements-expert's write scope covers only *-non-goal-*.md content, not the index). No system-design.md edit at triage: this slice extends VisitController's Contracts-row behavior and Implements set to REQ-VIS-003 - best reflected by doc-sync after implementation, not pre-committed here. Security posture unchanged: no auth exists app-wide (documented), and this slice introduces no new trust boundary beyond the path-variable scoping already covered by the mitigation above.

findings.description: processVisitEditFormSuccess asserts only that the pet's visit count stays at 1 after the edit POST. This pins the no-duplicate constraint but leaves the 'updates that same visit in place' half of the acceptance criterion untested. A silent binding failure — where the resident visit's date and description are not updated but no extra visit is created — would pass this test. After the MockMvc call completes, the resident visit in this.pet.getVisits() will already hold the bound values (MVC binding mutates the instance in place before the mocked save). The test should retrieve that visit and assert its date equals LocalDate.now().plusDays(3) and its description equals 'Follow-up examination'.

All four new test methods use implementation-method names instead of the BDD behavior school required by testing-principles.md § Test Naming ('the{Subject}Should{Outcome}', applies to tests written from 2026-07-31 onward): initVisitEditForm, processVisitEditFormSuccess, processVisitEditFormHasErrors, processVisitEditFormHasErrorsWhenVisitDateIsNotInFuture. Behavior names would be: theVisitEditFormShouldPrefillWithCurrentDateAndDescription, theVisitEditShouldUpdateInPlaceAndRedirectToOwner, theVisitEditShouldRejectBlankDescription, theVisitEditShouldRejectNonFutureDate.
findings.fix: Rename all four methods to the{Subject}Should{Outcome} form per the brief.

findings.description: The @BeforeEach block was modified in this slice and now constructs Owner, Pet, and Visit directly (new Owner(), new Pet(), new Visit() + setters). testing-principles.md § Factory Methods requires 'a slice touching a test moves that test's construction behind a factory.' The Visit construction (lines 73-77) is entirely new to this slice and should be wrapped in a factory method (e.g., createVisitWithId(int id, LocalDate date, String description)).
findings.fix: Extract a factory method for Visit construction that accepts id, date, and description; call it from @BeforeEach.
